results.title: Classes of invariant ideals are ambiguous
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be odd and squarefree, $\sigma$ the nontrivial automorphism of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ and $I$ a nonzero ideal of $\mathcal O$ with $\sigma I=I$. Then $[I]$ lies in the image of $\psi$.

results.title: Every class has a representative of norm prime to $q$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n\ge1$, $\mathcal O$ the ring of integers of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ and $q$ a prime. Every ideal class of $\mathcal O$ contains a nonzero ideal $I$ with $q\nmid N(I)$. Along the way, an ideal $I$ with $I+q\mathcal O=\mathcal O$ satisfies $q\nmid N(I)$.

results.title: Norms are squares modulo the primes of $n$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n\ge1$ be squarefree, $\mathcal O$ the ring of integers of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ and $q$ a prime dividing $n$. For every $x\in\mathcal O$, the norm $N(x)$ is a square modulo $q$. Hence $[N((x))/q]=0$ for every principal ideal $(x)$ of $\mathcal O$.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n\ge1$, $\mathrm{Cl}$ the class group of the ring of integers $\mathcal O$ of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$, and $q$ a prime dividing $n$. For each class $c\in\mathrm{Cl}$ fix a nonzero ideal $I_c\in c$ with $q\nmid N(I_c)$; one exists by the choice of representatives prime to $q$. results.title: Split primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n\ge1$, $\mathcal O$ the ring of integers of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$, and $p$ an odd prime with $p\nmid n$ such that $-n$ is a square modulo $p$. Then $\mathcal O$ has a nonzero ideal of norm $p$.

results.title: The genus characters take all allowed values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be odd and squarefree, and let $\varepsilon$ assign a bit $\varepsilon_q\in\mathbb F_2$ to each prime $q\mid n$, with $\sum_q\varepsilon_q=0$ if $n\equiv3\pmod4$. Then there is an ideal class $c$ of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ with $\chi_q(c)=\varepsilon_q$ for every prime $q\mid n$.
